questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following nanomaterials has one dimension $< 100$ nm?
questions.solution:
Nanomaterials are classified based on the number of dimensions that lie in the nanoscale range (1$ to 100$ nm).

Zero-dimensional (0D) nanomaterials have all three dimensions in the nanoscale. Examples include quantum dots and nanoparticles.

One-dimensional (1D) nanomaterials have two dimensions in the nanoscale. Examples include nanowires and nanotubes.

Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials have exactly one dimension in the nanoscale. Examples include thin films, graphene, and nanosheets.

Three-dimensional (3D) nanomaterials have no dimensions in the nanoscale but possess nanoscale features.

Since thin films have only one dimension (thickness) less than $100$ nm, they are classified as 2D nanomaterials.

Answer: Thin films

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the term used to describe movement of colloidal particles under applied electric potential without using semipermeable membrane.
questions.solution:
The movement of colloidal particles under the influence of an applied electric potential is called electrophoresis.

When the movement of colloidal particles is prevented by some suitable means (like a semipermeable membrane), it is observed that the dispersion medium begins to move in an electric field. This phenomenon is termed electroosmosis.

Since the question specifies the movement of colloidal particles without using a semipermeable membrane, the correct term is electrophoresis.

Answer: Electrophoresis

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ranges of particle size defines nano scale ?
questions.solution:
Nanoscale is defined as the size range from $1$ nm to $100$ nm.

Particles with at least one dimension in this size range are considered nanoparticles.

Answer: $1\text{-}100$ nm

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of following forces is responsible for physisorption ?
questions.solution:
Physisorption, also known as physical adsorption, arises due to weak van der Waals forces between the adsorbate and the adsorbent.

London force of dispersion is a type of van der Waals force and is the primary force responsible for physisorption.

Coulombic and electrostatic forces are strong forces typically associated with ionic interactions or chemisorption, while hydrogen bonding is a specific dipole-dipole interaction not universally responsible for physisorption.

Answer: London force of dispersion

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following properties of colloid is used to measure the rate of migration of sol particles?
questions.solution:
Electrophoresis is the phenomenon of movement of colloidal particles under the influence of an applied electric field. By observing this movement, the rate of migration of sol particles can be measured.

Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles.

Brownian motion is the continuous zig-zag motion of colloidal particles.

Electroosmosis is the movement of the dispersion medium under an electric field when the colloidal particles are prevented from moving.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of macromolecular colloid?
questions.solution:
Macromolecular colloids are formed when large molecules (macromolecules) having colloidal dimensions are dispersed in a suitable dispersion medium. Examples include naturally occurring macromolecules such as starch, cellulose, proteins, and enzymes, as well as man-made polymers like polythene, nylon, and polystyrene.

Soaps and detergents are examples of associated colloids (micelles), which are formed by the aggregation of a large number of ions in concentrated solutions.

Sulphur sol, consisting of particles containing a thousand or more $\text{S}_8$ sulphur molecules, is an example of a multimolecular colloid.

Therefore, proteins are an example of a macromolecular colloid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following anions has greater power for coagulation of positive sol?
questions.solution:
According to the Hardy-Schulze rule, the coagulating power of an ion is directly proportional to the magnitude of its charge (valency). For the coagulation of a positive sol, an anion is required.

The given anions and their charge magnitudes are:
$\text{Cl}^-$ : $1$
$\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ : $2$
$\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ (given as $\text{PO}_4^{2-}$ in options) : $3$
$[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ : $4$

Since $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ has the highest negative charge, it possesses the maximum coagulating power among the given options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is NOT an example of oil in water emulsion?
questions.solution:
Emulsions are broadly classified into two types based on the dispersed phase and dispersion medium:

1. Oil in water (O/W) emulsion: In this type, oil acts as the dispersed phase and water acts as the dispersion medium. Examples include milk, vanishing cream, and paint.

2. Water in oil (W/O) emulsion: In this type, water acts as the dispersed phase and oil acts as the dispersion medium. Examples include butter, cold cream, and cod liver oil.

Since butter is a water in oil (W/O) emulsion, it is not an example of an oil in water emulsion.

Answer: Butter

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a nanomaterial having all three dimensions less than 100 nm?
questions.solution:
Nanomaterials are classified based on the number of dimensions that are not confined to the nanoscale range (< 100$ nm).

Zero-dimensional (0D) nanomaterials have all three dimensions in the nanoscale range (less than 100$ nm). Examples include quantum dots, nanoparticles, and fullerenes.

One-dimensional (1D) nanomaterials have two dimensions in the nanoscale and one macroscopic dimension. Examples include nanotubes, nanowires, and nanofibers.

Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials have one dimension in the nanoscale and two macroscopic dimensions. Examples include thin films, graphene, and coatings.

Therefore, quantum dots are the nanomaterials having all three dimensions less than $100$ nm.

Answer: Quantum dots

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following properties is responsible for the development of colour to the colloids?
questions.solution:
The colour of a colloidal solution depends on the wavelength of light scattered by the dispersed particles.

The scattering of light by colloidal particles is known as the Tyndall effect.

Therefore, the Tyndall effect is responsible for the development of colour in colloids.

Answer: Tyndall effect

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Nano materials not applied in
questions.solution:
Nanomaterials are extensively used in the manufacturing of scratch-proof glasses, electronic devices, and self-cleaning materials (such as titanium dioxide nanoparticles).

Conventional water treatment relies on traditional physical and chemical processes like coagulation, flocculation, sedimentation, and sand filtration, which do not involve the use of nanomaterials. Advanced water treatment may use nanomaterials, but conventional methods do not.

Answer: Conventional water treatment

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following exhibits the minimum coagulating power for precipitating of positively charged ferric oxide sol ?
questions.solution:
According to the Hardy-Schulze rule, the coagulating power of an ion is directly proportional to the magnitude of its charge.

Since the ferric oxide sol is positively charged, the anions of the added electrolyte are responsible for its coagulation.

The anions provided by the given electrolytes are:
$\text{KNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{NO}_3^{-}$ (charge magnitude = $1$)
$\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{SO}_4^{2-}$ (charge magnitude = $2$)
$\text{K}_3\text{PO}_4 \rightarrow \text{PO}_4^{3-}$ (charge magnitude = $3$)
$\text{K}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6] \rightarrow [\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ (charge magnitude = $4$)

The order of coagulating power is $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-} > \text{PO}_4^{3-} > \text{SO}_4^{2-} > \text{NO}_3^{-}$.

Thus, $\text{KNO}_3$ exhibits the minimum coagulating power.

Answer: $\text{KNO}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the role of catalyst in catalytic reaction ?
options: It decreases the enthalpy of reaction.
It increases the enthalpy of reaction.
It decreases the energy of activation of reaction.
It increases the energy of activation of reaction.
questions.solution:
A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway that has a lower activation energy.

It does not alter the enthalpy, entropy, or Gibbs free energy of the reaction.

Thus, the primary role of a catalyst is to decrease the energy of activation of the reaction.

Answer: It decreases the energy of activation of reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is applicable to thin film?
questions.solution:
Nanostructures are classified based on the number of dimensions that are not confined to the nanoscale range (< 100$ nm).

Zero-dimensional (0D) nanostructures have all three dimensions in the nanoscale (e.g., quantum dots, nanoparticles).

One-dimensional (1D) nanostructures have two dimensions in the nanoscale and one extended dimension (e.g., nanowires, nanotubes).

Two-dimensional (2D) nanostructures have one dimension in the nanoscale (thickness) and two extended dimensions (length and width). A thin film falls under this category as its thickness is in the nanometer range while its other two dimensions are macroscopic.

Three-dimensional (3D) nanostructures have all three dimensions outside the nanoscale (e.g., bulk materials).

Therefore, a thin film is a two-dimensional nanostructure.

Answer: Two dimensional nanostructure$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II
List IList II
(A). Brownian Motion(I). Removal of impurities from the colloidal sols using a semipermeable membrane.
(B). Tyndall Effect(II). Movement of colloidal particles under the influence of an electric field.
(C). Electrophoresis(III). Random movement of colloidal particles due to kinetic energy.
(D). Dialysis(IV). Scattering of light by colloidal particles
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Brownian motion is the continuous random zig-zag movement of colloidal particles due to unequal bombardment by the molecules of the dispersion medium. Thus, (A) \rightarrow (III).

Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles, making the path of light visible. Thus, (B) \rightarrow (IV).

Electrophoresis is the movement of colloidal particles towards oppositely charged electrodes under the influence of an applied electric field. Thus, (C) \rightarrow (II).

Dialysis is the process of removing dissolved impurities from a colloidal sol using a semipermeable membrane. Thus, (D) \rightarrow (I).

The correct matching is (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (II), (D) - (I).

Answer: (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following nano structures includes nanotubes as an example?
questions.solution:
Nanomaterials are classified based on the number of dimensions that are outside the nanoscale range (greater than $100$ nm).

Zero-dimensional (0D) nanomaterials have all three dimensions in the nanoscale. Examples include quantum dots and nanoparticles.

One-dimensional (1D) nanomaterials have two dimensions in the nanoscale and one dimension outside the nanoscale. Examples include nanotubes, nanowires, and nanorods.

Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials have one dimension in the nanoscale and two dimensions outside the nanoscale. Examples include graphene and thin films.

Three-dimensional (3D) nanomaterials have no dimensions in the nanoscale but possess nanoscale features. Examples include bulk nanomaterials.

Since nanotubes have a nanoscale diameter but a macroscopic length, they are classified as one-dimensional nanostructures.

Answer: One dimensional

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a water-in-oil type of emulsion?
questions.solution:
Emulsions are colloidal systems in which both the dispersed phase and the dispersion medium are liquids.

In a water-in-oil (W/O) emulsion, water is the dispersed phase and oil is the dispersion medium.

Butter is an example of a water-in-oil emulsion, where water is dispersed in fat (oil).

Milk and vanishing cream are examples of oil-in-water (O/W) emulsions, where oil is dispersed in water.

Answer: Butter

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct statement regarding lyophilic colloid from the following.
options: It is formed only by special methods.
questions.solution:
The word lyophilic means liquid-loving or solvent-loving. Therefore, lyophilic colloids are solvent-loving colloids.

They are reversible in nature because if the dispersion medium is separated from the dispersed phase, the sol can be reconstituted by simply remixing with the dispersion medium.

They can be prepared easily by directly mixing the dispersed phase with the dispersion medium, without requiring any special methods.

Answer: It is solvent loving colloid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct for the spontaneous adsorption of a gas?
options: $\Delta S$ is negative and, therefore $\Delta H$ should be highly positive
$\Delta S$ is negative and therefore, $\Delta H$ should be highly negative.
$\Delta S$ is positive and therefore, $\Delta H$ should be negative.
$\Delta S$ is positive and therefore, $\Delta H$ should also be highly positive.
questions.solution:
During the adsorption of a gas, the gas molecules are restricted to the surface of the solid, which decreases their randomness or entropy. Thus, the change in entropy, $\Delta S$, is negative.

For a process to be spontaneous, the change in Gibbs free energy, $\Delta G$, must be negative.

According to the Gibbs-Helmholtz equation:
$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$

Since $\Delta S$ is negative, the term $-T\Delta S$ becomes positive. For $\Delta G$ to be negative, the enthalpy change, $\Delta H$, must be negative and its magnitude must be large enough to overcome the positive $-T\Delta S$ term.

Therefore, $\Delta S$ is negative and $\Delta H$ should be highly negative.

Answer: $\Delta S$ is negative and therefore, $\Delta H$ should be highly negative.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the dimensional nature of nanoparticles by the following.
questions.solution:
Nanomaterials are classified based on the number of dimensions that are not confined to the nanoscale range (1-100$ nm).

Zero-dimensional (0$D) nanomaterials have all three dimensions in the nanoscale. Examples include nanoparticles, quantum dots, and fullerenes.

One-dimensional (1$D) nanomaterials have two dimensions in the nanoscale. Examples include nanotubes and nanowires.

Two-dimensional (2$D) nanomaterials have one dimension in the nanoscale. Examples include graphene and nanofilms.

Since nanoparticles have all three dimensions in the nanoscale, they are classified as zero-dimensional.

Answer: zero dimensional

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the gas adsorbed by solid to the largest extent at their respective critical temperature.
questions.solution:
The extent of adsorption of a gas on a solid surface depends on the strength of intermolecular forces. Gases with higher critical temperatures have stronger van der Waals forces of attraction and are more easily liquefiable, leading to a greater extent of adsorption.

The critical temperatures of the given gases are approximately:
$\text{H}_{2} \approx 33 \text{ K}$
$\text{N}_{2} \approx 126 \text{ K}$
$\text{O}_{2} \approx 154 \text{ K}$
$\text{SO}_{2} \approx 430 \text{ K}$

Since $\text{SO}_{2}$ has the highest critical temperature among the given options, it has the strongest intermolecular forces and is adsorbed to the largest extent.

Answer: $\text{SO}_{2(g)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following nanomaterial has all the three dimensions $< 100$ nm?
questions.solution:
Nanomaterials are classified based on the number of dimensions that are in the nanoscale range (1$ to 100$ nm).

Zero-dimensional (0D) nanomaterials have all three dimensions in the nanoscale (< 100$ nm). Examples include nanoparticles, quantum dots, and nanoshells.

One-dimensional (1D) nanomaterials have two dimensions in the nanoscale and one dimension outside the nanoscale. Examples include nanotubes and nanowires.

Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials have one dimension in the nanoscale and two dimensions outside the nanoscale. Examples include thin films and coatings.

Since nanoshells are zero-dimensional nanomaterials, they have all three dimensions less than 100$ nm.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following assertions about the extent of physisorption is correct?
options: Decreases with increase in surface area
Decreases with increase in the strength of Van der Waals forces
questions.solution:
Physisorption is an exothermic process. According to Le Chatelier's principle, an increase in temperature shifts the equilibrium in the backward direction, leading to desorption. Thus, the extent of physisorption decreases with an increase in temperature.

Additionally, the extent of physisorption increases with an increase in the surface area of the adsorbent and with an increase in the strength of Van der Waals forces between the adsorbate and adsorbent.

Answer: Decreases with increase in temperature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a characterstic of chemisorption?
options: Heat released is in the range of $40-200 \mathrm{ kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$.
Formation of multimolecular layer of adsorbate.
questions.solution:
Identify which option is not a characteristic of chemisorption:

Chemisorption involves the formation of chemical bonds between adsorbate and adsorbent, making it highly specific—option (A) is characteristic.

The heat released is typically in the range $40-200 \mathrm{ kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$, aligning with chemical bond energies—option (B) is characteristic.

Chemisorption is unimolecular; strong covalent bonds occupy surface sites, preventing multilayer formation, which is a trait of physisorption—option (C) is not characteristic.

The process is irreversible due to high activation energy for desorption—option (D) is characteristic.

The answer is $\boxed{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify catalyst used in following reaction.
$\mathrm{CO}_{(\mathrm{g})}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{g})} \xrightarrow{623 \mathrm{ K}} \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{ g})}+\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{ g})}$
questions.solution:
Water-Gas Shift Reaction: $\mathrm{CO}_{(\mathrm{g})}+\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{g})} \xrightarrow{623 \mathrm{ K}} \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{ g})}+\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{ g})}$

The reaction at 623 K represents the high-temperature water-gas shift process, which employs iron oxide-chromium oxide catalysts (iron chromate) to enhance hydrogen production and reduce carbon monoxide.

Among the options, vanadium pentoxide catalyzes sulfuric acid production, nickel metal facilitates hydrogenation and reforming, and acid/alkali traces serve other catalytic purposes. Iron chromate remains the standard catalyst for this specific industrial process.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{A}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the negatively charged sol from following.
questions.solution:
The charge on colloidal particles arises from preferential ion adsorption, electron capture during electro-dispersion, or dissociation of surface molecules.

Colloidal sols exhibit either positive or negative net charges:

Negatively charged sols: Metal sulfides (As_2S_3$, $CdS$), acidic dyes (Eosin, Congo red), starch, gum, clay, charcoal, and metals (Au$, $Ag$, $Pt$).

Positively charged sols: Metal hydroxides (Fe(OH)_3$, $Al(OH)_3$), basic dyes (Methylene blue), and haemoglobin under specific pH conditions.

Analyzing the options: Eosin is an acidic dye with deprotonated groups, yielding negative charges. Titanium oxide (TiO_2$) typically adsorbs positive ions. Methylene blue, a basic dye, protonates to form positive charges. Haemoglobin, being amphoteric, varies with pH but is often positive in acidic conditions.

Eosin definitively forms a negatively charged sol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following nanomaterial has all three dimensions less than 100 nm ?
questions.solution:
Nanomaterials are classified by the number of dimensions confined to the nanoscale (less than 100 nm). Zero-dimensional (0D) nanomaterials have all three dimensions confined to the nanoscale; examples include nanoparticles, quantum dots, and nanoshells. One-dimensional (1D) nanomaterials have two nanoscale dimensions with a larger third dimension—nanotubes, nanowires, and nanofibers exhibit this structure. Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials feature one nanoscale dimension and two larger dimensions, as seen in thin films, coatings, and graphene. Three-dimensional (3D) nanomaterials have all dimensions larger than 100 nm but contain internal nanoscale features, such as bulk nanostructured materials and composites.

Nanoshells, with a dielectric core and metallic shell, are spherical and have all dimensions (diameter) typically under 100 nm, classifying them as 0D nanomaterials. Nanotubes and nanofibers, with nanoscale diameters but macroscopic lengths, are 1D. Thin films, with nanoscale thickness but large length and width, are 2D. Thus, only nanoshells have all three dimensions less than 100 nm.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which instrument is used for determination of particle size?
questions.solution:
Particle size determination requires direct imaging capabilities provided by electron microscopy techniques. SEM offers surface visualization for measuring particle dimensions through high-resolution topography, while TEM achieves higher resolution for nanoscale internal structure analysis and particle measurement.

Spectroscopic methods prove unsuitable for direct size determination: FTIR identifies functional groups and chemical composition, and UV-visible spectroscopy quantifies concentrations and electronic transitions, though it may provide indirect size information through plasmon resonance effects in specific cases.

The instruments directly capable of particle size determination are $\boxed{\text{A, B}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following gases is least adsorbed on solid at similar conditions of temperature and pressure?
questions.solution:
The extent of physisorption depends directly on a gas's ease of liquefaction, which is governed by intermolecular forces and critical temperature. Stronger intermolecular forces and higher critical temperatures correspond to greater adsorption.

Examining the gases: $\mathrm{SO}_2$ ($T_c = 157.5^{}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$) exhibits significant dipole-dipole interactions; $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ ($T_c = 144^{}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$) experiences strong London dispersion forces; $\mathrm{NH}_3$ ($T_c = 132.4^{}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$) forms hydrogen bonds; $\mathrm{H}_2$ ($T_c = -239.9^{}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$) has minimal intermolecular forces due to its small size and nonpolar nature.

Since $\mathrm{H}_2$ has the lowest critical temperature and weakest intermolecular interactions, it is the least easily liquefied and consequently the least adsorbed.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the technique used to know binding nature of nanomaterials?
questions.solution: The binding nature of nanomaterials refers to their chemical bonds and functional groups. Electron microscopy techniques like SEM and TEM reveal morphological and structural features but not chemical bonding. XRD determines crystal structure and phase composition. Only FTIR spectroscopy directly identifies functional groups through characteristic infrared absorption frequencies.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following substances is classified as macromolecular colloid?
questions.solution:
Colloid classification depends on the dispersed phase particle structure. Multimolecular colloids form from aggregates of small molecules (e.g., gold sol), while macromolecular colloids consist of individual large molecules like proteins or synthetic polymers. Associated colloids (micelles) form aggregates only at higher concentrations, as with soaps.

Analyzing the options: soap and detergent form micelles (associated colloids), $\text{S}_8$ sulfur aggregates into multimolecular colloids, and nylon exists as individual macromolecules of colloidal size.

Nylon is therefore a macromolecular colloid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the temperature from following graph so that highest amount of a gas is adsorbed
questions.solution:
Adsorption isotherms plot the extent of adsorption $(x/m)$ against pressure $(p)$ at constant temperatures. Since adsorption is exothermic, Le Chatelier's principle indicates that lower temperatures favor greater adsorption.

The graph contains four isotherms labeled 195 K, 210 K, 244 K, and 273 K. The topmost curve, corresponding to 195 K, shows the highest $(x/m)$ values across all pressures, confirming that maximum adsorption occurs at the lowest temperature.

$\boxed{195\text{ K}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of colloid the fog is ?
questions.solution:
The classification depends on the states of the dispersed phase and dispersion medium. In fog, a liquid (water droplets) is dispersed in a gas (air), which forms a liquid aerosol.

Other examples include mist and clouds. Conversely, foam is a gas in a liquid, gel is a liquid in a solid, and emulsion is a liquid in a liquid.

$\therefore$ The correct option is $\mathbf{A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is classified as multimolecular colloid?
questions.solution:
Multimolecular colloids result from the aggregation of numerous small molecules or atoms into colloidal-sized particles. Individual components possess diameters below 1 nm, while the aggregated particles fall within the 1–1000 nm colloidal range.

Evaluating the options: starch and cellulose are macromolecular colloids composed of large polymer molecules intrinsically at colloidal scale. Plastics similarly constitute macromolecular colloidal systems.

S_8$ sulfur molecules demonstrate distinct behavior. When dissolved in alcohol and introduced to water, sulfur undergoes aggregation. Though individual S_8$ molecules are sub-colloidal, their association produces particles meeting colloidal dimensional criteria. This aggregation mechanism classifies sulfur as a multimolecular colloid.

The correct identification is C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ion exihibits maximum power of coagulation for positively charged sol?
questions.solution:
Coagulating power depends on the valency of the active ion, as per the Hardy-Schulze rule.

For positively charged sols, anions serve as the active ions. Comparing valencies:

A) $\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$: valency 2
B) $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$: valency 1
C) $\mathrm{PO}_4^{3-}$: valency 3
D) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$: valency 4

Since coagulating power increases with valency, the highest valency (4) corresponds to maximum coagulation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following process does NOT results in coagulation?
options: by mixing two oppositely charged sols
questions.solution:
Coagulation is the aggregation of colloidal particles into larger masses that sediment, following destabilization of the sol. Electrophoresis induces coagulation via charge neutralization at electrodes, boiling disrupts stabilizing layers through thermal agitation, and mixing oppositely charged sols causes mutual neutralization. Adding excess solvent, however, generally stabilizes the sol by reducing particle collision frequencies and diluting coagulating electrolytes, rather than promoting aggregation.

Thus, adding excess solvent does not typically result in coagulation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following represents the Freundlich's empirical equation for adsorption of gas on solid (for $\mathrm{n} > 1$)
questions.solution:
The Freundlich adsorption isotherm provides an empirical relationship describing the amount of gas adsorbed per unit mass of solid adsorbent in terms of pressure at a fixed temperature, expressed as

$\frac{x}{m} = kP^{\frac{1}{n}}$

where $x$ is the mass of the adsorbate, $m$ the mass of the adsorbent, and $P$ the pressure. Constants $k$ and $n$ (with $n > 1$) characterize the adsorbent-adsorbate system.

Comparing with the options: Option A matches the Freundlich isotherm exactly. Option B erroneously inverts the ratio $\frac{x}{m}$ to $\frac{m}{x}$. Option C uses an exponent of $n$ instead of $\frac{1}{n}$, and option D combines both errors.

The correct representation is $\boxed{A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify sequential reactions involved in Sol-Gel process.
questions.solution:
The sol-gel process involves two sequential reactions for producing solid materials from molecular precursors.

Hydrolysis replaces alkoxy groups with hydroxyl groups:
$\mathrm{M(OR)_n + xH_2 O \rightarrow M(OH)_x(OR)_{n-x} + xROH}$

Polycondensation follows, forming metal-oxygen-metal bridges through either olation/oxolation or esterification:
$\mathrm{M-OH + HO-M \rightarrow M-O-M + H_2 O}$
$\mathrm{M-OR + HO-M \rightarrow M-O-M + ROH}$

This sequence establishes the correct order as hydrolysis followed by polycondensation, corresponding to option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the property of colloidal solutions so that colloidal particles move freely towards respective electrodes under an applied electrical potential.
questions.solution:
Electrophoresis describes the movement of charged colloidal particles toward oppositely charged electrodes under an applied electric potential.

Colloidal particles carry surface charges, causing migration in an electric field. Brownian motion involves random thermal movement without directional bias. Electroosmosis concerns fluid movement relative to fixed charged surfaces. Dialysis removes dissolved impurities through selective diffusion.

The described behavior aligns precisely with electrophoresis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following gases is adsorbed to greater extent if adsorbent remains same at similar conditions of temperature and pressure?
questions.solution:
The extent of adsorption in physisorption depends on the ease of gas liquefaction, which correlates directly with critical temperature $T_c$.

The critical temperatures are: $\mathrm{H}_2$ at 33 K, $\mathrm{N}_2$ at 126 K, $\mathrm{O}_2$ at 155 K, and $\mathrm{SO}_2$ at 430.65 K.

Increasing order of $T_c$ is $\mathrm{H}_2 < \mathrm{N}_2 < \mathrm{O}_2 < \mathrm{SO}_2$.

$\mathrm{SO}_2$ has the highest critical temperature and will thus be adsorbed most extensively.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is effectively used to remove E. coli bacteria from water?
questions.solution:
Silver nanoparticles exhibit potent antimicrobial properties through several mechanisms that effectively eliminate E. coli. Silver ions $\mathrm{Ag^+}$ disrupt bacterial cell membrane integrity, penetrate cells to interfere with metabolic pathways, inhibit enzyme activity, and damage DNA.

Carbon black nanoparticles primarily function as adsorbents without significant intrinsic antimicrobial effects. Titanium dioxide nanoparticles $\mathrm{TiO_2}$ require UV activation for photocatalytic generation of reactive oxygen species. Silicon nanoparticles lack effective antimicrobial properties for direct bacterial removal.

Silver nanoparticles provide direct, light-independent antimicrobial action, making them the optimal choice for E. coli removal from water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not negatively charged sol?
questions.solution:
Charge determination for colloidal systems

Colloidal charge arises from preferential ion adsorption from solution or intrinsic molecular properties.

The $\mathrm{As}_2\mathrm{S}_3$ sol adsorbs sulfide ions ($\mathrmS^{2-} ) resulting in negative charge.

Clay particles develop negative charge through isomorphic substitution (\mathrm{Al}^{3+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$) and surface hydroxyl dissociation.

Congo Red, an anionic dye, forms negatively charged colloidal particles through adsorption of dye anions.

Haemoglobin exhibits amphoteric behavior with isoelectric point near pH 6.8-7.1. Below this pH, amino group protonation yields net positive charge, distinguishing it from consistently negative sols.

$\mathrm{As}_2\mathrm{S}_3, clay, and Congo Red sols are negatively charged, while haemoglobin is not.

The answer is $\boxed{B}$.

$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify example of sorption from following.
options: Charcol is added to methylene blue solution.
Hydrogen gas is passed over platinum.
Oxygen gas is passed over finely divided nickel.
questions.solution:
Sorption describes the uptake of one substance by another, encompassing both adsorption and absorption. Adsorption involves accumulation on a surface, while absorption involves uniform distribution throughout a bulk material.

In the given examples: charcoal with methylene blue shows adsorption of dye molecules on the surface; chalk dipped in ink shows absorption as ink penetrates the bulk; hydrogen over platinum and oxygen over finely divided nickel both demonstrate adsorption of gases onto metal surfaces.

All processes are types of sorption.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match column I (process) with column II (application)
Column IColumn II
A)Dialysisa)Cleansing action of soap
B)Peptizationb)Coagulation
C)Emulsificationc)Colloidal Solution Preparation
D)Electrophoresisd)Purification of colloidal solution
questions.solution:
Matching the processes with their applications:

Dialysis purifies colloidal solutions using a semi-permeable membrane, matching with (d).

Peptization forms colloids from precipitates with an electrolyte, matching with (c).

Emulsification disperses immiscible liquids, fundamental to the cleansing action of soap, matching with (a).

Electrophoresis moves charged colloids to electrodes causing coagulation, matching with (b).

Thus, $A \to d$, $B \to c$, $C \to a$, $D \to b$, corresponding to option B.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a first step in mechanism of heterogenous catalysis?
options: Desorption of reaction product from catalyst surface
Adsorption of reactant molecules on catalyst surface to form an intermediate
Occurrence of chemical reaction on catalyst surface to form an intermediate
Diffusion of reactants towards catalyst surface
questions.solution:
The catalytic activity is localised on the surface of the catalyst. The mechanism involves five steps:
(i) Diffusion of reactants to the surface of the catalyst.
(ii) Adsorption of reactant molecules on the surface of the catalyst.
(iii) Occurrence of chemical reaction on the catalyst surface, through formation of an intermediate.
(iv) Desorption of reaction products away from the catalyst surface.
(v) Diffusion of reaction products away from the catalyst surface.

In the human body, the carbonic anhydrase enzyme catalyses the reaction of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ with water. It catalyses a reaction that converts $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ and water into carbonic acid, which dissociates into protons and bicarbonate ions. It is found in red blood cells.
$\mathrm{CO}_{2}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} \stackrel{\text{ Carbonic anhydrase }}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{CO}_{3}\mathrm{CO}_{2}  is transported from tissues to the lungs through the bloodstream.$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a character of catalyst?
options: It changes the position of equilibrium.
It increases the rates of both forward and Backward reactions equally in reversible reaction.
It affects the energies of reactants and products of the reaction.
It increases the activation energy of reactants.
questions.solution: Reactions can be sped up by the addition of a catalyst, including reversible reactions involving a final equilibrium state. Recall that for a reversible reaction, the equilibrium state is one in which the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal. In the presence of a catalyst, both the forward and reverse reaction rates will speed up equally, thereby allowing the system to reach equilibrium faster. However, it is very important to keep in mind that the addition of a catalyst has no effect whatsoever on the final equilibrium position of the reaction. It simply gets it there faster.
